contexts.text: They shall build the wastes of eternity, and they shall erect the olden desolations, and they shall renew the cities of the waste, the desolations of generation and of generation (). Wastes = evils; desolations, falsities.
In the Prophets, that is called wasting (or vastation) which regards the celestial things of faith; and desolation, that which regards the spiritual things of faith. Illustrated.
Wound = that faith is desolated; bruise, that charity is devastated.
The waters which they shall drink in desolation () = the spiritual things to which they have done violence, or which they have profaned.

By the Flood is also signified the desolation of those who were not able to be regenerated. Both temptations and desolations are compared in the Word to floods or inundations of waters. (Illustrated as to both temptations and desolations.)

The reason both temptations and desolations are compared to floods... is that the case is similar. It is evil Spirits who flow in with their persuasions and principles of falsity... But with the man who is being regenerated there are temptations; and with the man who is not being regenerated there are desolations.
Desolations and temptations are nothing but inundations of the falsities which are excited by evil Spirits.
Desolation is an expression which relates to spiritual things; vastation, to celestial things.
In temptations there are vastations and desolations...
In the Prophets, when it treats of vastation and desolation, it is said that they wail and cry.
The desolation of faith, which is effected by means of falsities. Treated of.
The abomination of desolation () = the state of the Church when there is no love and no charity. When these are desolated, there reign abominable things.
That there is vastation is evident, for it is said, a desolation to eternity ().
(Hagar's) water consumed () = the desolation of truth (with the spiritual). AC 2689, Explained. AC 2694.
The desolation of truth treated of in ; .
These words (concerning Hagar) involve the state of thought of those who are in the desolation of truth and in consequent despair.

They who are being reformed are reduced into ignorance of truth, or desolation, even to grief and despair, and then first they have comfort and help from the Lord... They who are such that they can be reformed, if not in the bodily life, in the other life, are brought into this state, which in the other life is very well known, and is called vastation or desolation. They who are in such vastation or desolation, are reduced to despair, and when they are in this state, they receive comfort and help from the Lord, and are at last carried thence into Heaven... The cause of this vastation and desolation is chiefly that the Persuasive may be broken which they have taken from proprium; also that they may receive the perception of good and truth, which they cannot do, until that Persuasive is softened... Example(s).

The first state after desolation is described in the preceding verse, which was a state of consolation and of the hope of aid. Their second state after desolation is described in this verse, which is a state of enlightenment and of recreation thence. Explained.
The desolation of truth; and afterwards the consolation, recreation, and instruction after desolation, are treated of in .
The land of the north () = ignorance or desolation of truth; weeping and prayers, their state of grief and despair; to be brought to fountains of waters, recreation and instruction in truths.
Wilderness () = the desolation of truth; waters, etc., = the truths which were for recreation and joy with those who have been in vastation.

Wilderness... = those who are in vastation as to good, and in desolation as to truth. This wilderness is predicated in a twofold sense, namely, of those who are afterwards reformed, and of those who cannot be reformed. Illustrated.

The journeyings and wanderings of the Israelitish people in the wilderness, represented nothing else than the vastation and desolation of the faithful before reformation, thus their temptation; since when they are in spiritual temptations, they are in vastation and desolation. Illustrated.
The gladness which is desolated () = is predicated of truth... Hence it is evident what is signified by what is left in the city is a desolation ().
All the gates (of Zion) are desolated () = that all the approaches are beset by falsities.
The inhabited cities shall be laid waste, and the Land shall be desolated (). The Land = the Church itself, which is said to be laid waste as to good; and desolated, as to truth.

To pass the night in the forest = to be desolated as to good... To pass the night in the forests there = to be no longer in goods, whence comes desolation, which is also described by wandering before the swords, before the outstretched sword.
To make them a desolation ()... Here, the desolation of the Spiritual Church is treated of.
A voice shall sing in the window = the desolation of truth, thus of the intellectual faculty as to truth.

When ye shall see the abomination of desolation = the vastation of the Church. Explained... When these things are in the Church, or rather in the tract where the Word is; that is, in the thought of the heart, although not in the doctrine of the lips, then there is desolation; and these things here mentioned are its abomination.
Here, now, it is the third state which is treated of, which is that of the desolation of the Church as to good and truth.
An eagle hastening to devour = to desolate man as to truths; for the desolation of the Church is here treated of.
The desolation of truth is called affliction in the Word throughout.
The state when man is apparently deprived of truths, is called desolation.
There is here described (by the seven years of famine) a state of desolation through the privation of truth; the last of this state is despair. Explained. AC 5280.
A state of the multiplication of truth from good... before the state of desolation which is signified by the years of famine. Signified.

The seven years of famine began to come = the following states of desolation... Famine = the lack of the Knowledges of truth and good, thus desolation. The reason famine = this lack, or desolation, is that there is no other celestial and spiritual food but good and truth... When, therefore, such things are lacking, there is famine, and in the Word it is called desolation and vastation; desolation, when truths are lacking; and vastation, when goods are lacking. In many places in the Word this desolation and vastation are treated of, and are there described by the desolation of the land, of kingdoms, of cities, of nations, of peoples; and it is also called exinanition, excision, consummation, wilderness, emptiness; and the very state itself is called the great day of Jehovah, etc. (Under Day, see this reference.)

This last state of the Church, which precedes the state of the New Church, is what is properly meant and described in the Word by vastation and desolation. By desolation and vastation in the Word there is also described the state which precedes the regeneration of man; which state is here signified by the seven years of famine.
The famine was in all lands = desolation everywhere in the Natural.
The famine was upon all the faces of the land = when there was desolation even to despair.
The height and the last of desolation is despair.
The famine prevailed in the land of Egypt = the increasing grievousness of the desolation in the Natural.
The famine prevailed in every land = that everywhere but there, there was desolation in the Natural.
How the case is with the desolation of the Natural, or with the privation of truth there. Explained.

When they come nearer to the very act of regeneration, they are as it were deprived of these truths, for they are drawn inwards, and then the man appears to be in desolation; but still these truths are successively remitted into the Natural... But with those who are not being regenerated... these truths are cast out... This state is also called desolation or vastation; but it differs from the former in that the desolation of the former state is only apparent, whereas the desolation of this state is absolute; for in the former state the man is not deprived of truths, whereas in this state he is utterly deprived of them. Concerning the desolation of the former state, it has treated in this chapter, and it treats further in the following one; and this is what is signified by the seven years of famine. The same desolation is frequently treated of elsewhere in the Word. Illustrated.

How the case is with desolation, is manifest from those who are in desolation in the other life. They who are in desolation there, are harassed by evil Spirits and Genii; for these infuse persuasions of evil and falsity, so that they are almost inundated; hence truths do not appear; but as the time of desolation is ended, they are enlightened by light from Heaven. Signified.

In this whole chapter () it treats of the desolation of those who are being regenerated; and of regeneration and fructification after desolation; and at last of the punishment of those who have oppressed. Further illustrated.
Desolation is for the sake of the end that man may be regenerated, that is, that after evils and falsities have been separated, truths may be conjoined with goods, and goods with truths.

The vastation and desolation of the man of the Church, or of the Church with man, was represented by the captivity of the Jewish people in Babylon... for desolation is captivity, as man is then kept as it were bound; wherefore by those bound, in prison, in the pit, are signified those who are in desolation.

The state of desolation and vastation with those who are not being regenerated, is also treated of in the Word throughout. In this state are those who altogether deny truths, or turn them into falsities. This is the state of the Church about the end. Illustrated.
Because the famine was in the Land of Canaan = that there was desolation as to those things which are of the Church in the Natural. Famine = the lack of Knowledges, and consequent desolation.
And the famine grew heavier = the desolation from the need of spiritual things.
The desolation of truth is treated of in .
When spiritual food is wanting to Good Spirits and Angels, they are in desolation...
The famine was very grievous = desolation.

As to desolation, it is to be known, that truths and goods, and the Knowledges of them, make the spiritual life of those who are in Heaven; they are their celestial and spiritual food, with which they are nourished... but when it is evening, they are lacking... This state is signified by famine, and it is a species of desolation, but not such as is with those in the Lower Earth.
That a true Scientific was no longer visible in the Natural and within the Church on account of the desolation. Signified.
Truth is said not to be visible, because in a state of desolation truth appears to have fled away; yet it is present... But in a state of desolation it is obscured by proprium...
This year was ended = desolation after the period of this state.
The good of truth... in like manner no longer visible on account of the desolation. Signified.
That the receptacles of good and truth were altogether desolated. Signified.
That if they were desolated, there would no longer be spiritual life under the Internal. Signified.
To die = desolation, that is, the privation of good and truth, which make the spiritual life.
The man who is being regenerated, is at last so reduced by repeated desolations and supports, that he no longer wants to be his own...
The famine prevailed over them = desolation even to despair...

By desolations and temptations, also, states contrary to heavenly life are perceived, and thus a sense and perception of the happiness of heavenly life is implanted... Therefore desolations and temptations are brought to their height, that is, to despair, in order that full relations may be had.
The whole Land shall be in desolation, in devastation, and these nations shall serve the king of Babel seventy years (). Seventy years = a full state of desolation and devastation.

In , there is described a state of temptations; the waters = falsities... the deep = the evil of falsity; the weeds wrapped around the head = that false scientifics were obsessing truth and good: so the case is in a state of desolations.
When a man shall desolate a field or a vineyard () = the deprivation of the good and truth of the Church through cupidities. To desolate = to deprive through cupidities.

And shall desolate in the field of another () = the consumption of cohering goods. To desolate = to deprive through cupidities, thus to consume... The reason to desolate (has this signification) is that the word by which to desolate is expressed in the Original Language, properly means to kindle and burn, thus also to eat up and consume; and as this is the derivation of this word, to desolate here = the consumption which takes place through cupidities; for the cupidities with man are fires which consume.
Thus is described (in ) the consumption and desolation of good and truth through cupidities.

Lest peradventure the Land be desolate () = deficiency in such a case, and little of spiritual life... For desolate, when said concerning the Church in man, = the lack of truth and good, thus also the lack of spiritual life. AE 650:59.
To desolate the earth and the fulness thereof () = to destroy all things of the Church.

It here treats () of the Advent of the Lord and of the state of the Church then, that there will be a desolation of all things of spiritual truth and good... The rivers of desolations = the truths of doctrine utterly desolated.
Which state of the Church is called consummation, devastation, desolation, and decision.

They shall make her desolate and naked () = that they will divest themselves of her falsities and evils... Desolation in the Word is predicated of truths and falsities; and nakedness of goods and evils.
The abomination of desolation = the falsification and deprivation of all truth.

The infestation of truth by falsities, even until there is no truth remaining which is not falsified and consummated... is meant by the abomination of desolation there: this is meant also by the desolation upon the bird of abominations, in Daniel. TCR 755.
The desolation of truth and the theological leanness in the Christian world at this day. Described.
From that time there commenced and increased the desolation foretold in Daniel and Matthew.

Vastation, desolation, decision, have a similar signification to consummation; but desolation = the consummation of truth; vastation, the consummation of good; and decision, the plenary consummation of both.

I will give the Land a desolation and a waste ()... The desolation and vastation of this = the last state of the Spiritual Church, which was when there was no longer any truth because there was no good, or when there was no faith because there was no charity; desolation is said of the truth which is of faith; and vastation, of the good which is of charity.

The destruction of all the goods of the Church, is signified by I will cut off the nations, and by their corners shall be desolated ()... The destruction of the truths of doctrine is signified by I will desolate their streets, and by their cities shall be desolated.
Great grief on account of the desolation of Divine truth in the Church. Signified.
In the following things of this chapter () it treats of the desolation of Divine truth in the Church.
A man and his brother shall be desolated () = faith and charity... To be desolated = the plenary extinction of both.
The flocks of small cattle are desolated () = the lack of the spiritual truth and good which are of faith and charity.

That all things of the Church and all things of the doctrine of the Church will perish, is signified by they shall be devastated in the midst of the devastated lands, and her cities in the midst of the desolate cities ().
Under Cup, see this reference.

Unto the end of the war the desolations are determined () = the falsification of truth until there is no longer any combat between truth and falsity... Desolation = the last time of the Church, when there is no longer any truth, but mere falsity.

More are the sons of the desolate one than the sons of the married one (). It here treats of a new Church to be established with the gentiles; the latter are signified by... the desolate one who shall have many sons.
The cities which are desolate () = doctrinal things without truths.

To make the desolate cities inhabited () = the life according to Divine truths of those things which heretofore had been destroyed... Desolate cities = these truths heretofore destroyed; namely, with the Jewish nation.
A lamentation by God concerning the desolation of truth in the Church ().
Devastation is predicated of good; desolation, of truth.
The cities which are desolated () = that there are no longer doctrinal things of truth.
On the abomination of desolation. General article.

The Novitiates asked, How can these things be called the abomination of desolation? The Angels replied, All these are in falsities as to faith and in evils as to life; the interiors of their minds are infernal... and as they are in the midst between the Heavens where the Angels are and the earth where men are, no Divine truth can pass from the Lord through the Heavens to the men of the Earth...
Redemption. 4. 1. The successive decrease of good and truth and increase of evil and falsity in the Church is called vastation and desolation.
Trinity. 9. Hence is that affliction and that desolation in the Christian Church, foretold by the Lord in the Evangelists and in Daniel.
No one can see the desolation of truth in the Church until truths from the Word come into light...
This state of the Church is described by vastation, desolation, and consummation.
Desolation = this falsification.
